_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Choosing the optimal execution path before starting work — plan-vs-act gates, agent-architecture selection (chaining,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "this task has failed twice, I need a fresh approach not another retry on the same path"
cases.context: The agent has access to the task-path-optimization skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is task-path-optimization the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes task-path-optimization as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against prioritization, context-engineering, tool-call-strategy
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the task-path-optimization workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore task-path-optimization
Does not route to prioritization, context-engineering, tool-call-strategy when the task-path-optimization scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "reduce the number of tool calls in this read-heavy step"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should task-path-optimization be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside task-path-optimization's ownership
Routes the work to prioritization or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying task-path-optimization terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply task-path-optimization as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if task-path-optimization has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim task-path-optimization should own the request
Does not use task-path-optimization's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
